findings.reason: without a reproduction of the cited defect the node's negative control cannot fire, and a worker would discover only at the gate that its fixture proves nothing.
findings.text: §18's fixture prints "warning lines naming a test node and a `warnings summary` block", but a pytest warnings summary line never begins with `FAILED` or `ERROR` and so is not read as a failing id by the parser the negative control restores; the cited defect line is `ERROR    imas_codex.standard_names.export:export.py:3553 Withholding a from catalog export: …` in `head-suite-archive.log:145`, a logging record that the base parser matches only because of its `ERROR` prefix on the next line's start. A fixture built as described cannot make the first case fail at base, so the done-when measures nothing.

findings.reason: the plan's own fixture design follows from the stated cause, so a misnamed cause is what produces the fixture that cannot fail.
findings.text: §18's Why calls the misread lines "two warning lines printed by `tests/standard_names/test_catalog_layout_hierarchy.py::TestOrderingCycleDetection`", and its Deliverable says "a warning summary included" is never read as a failing id, but the evidence in that run's head arm log is `ERROR    imas_codex.standard_names.export:export.py:3553 Withholding a from catalog export: hierarchy cycle relationships: …` (line 145), a logging record whose `ERROR` prefix is the whole cause: `_pytest_failure_ids` reads a log through `_GATE_FAILURE_RE = ^(?:FAILED|ERROR)\s+(.+)$` (`reckon/crew/review.py:1797`, `reckon/crew/review.py:2186`), and the review record's `added_failure_ids` for that run are exactly those two logging strings. Naming the cause as a warning directs the reader at pytest's warnings summary, which the reader already ignores; the endpoint still excludes printed lines, however it is described.
